smell: The codebase still uses the `prefix: message` convention ('update-ingress:', 'haproxy:', 'kubevip:', 'cluster:', 'cleanup:', 'terraform:', 'coreos:', 'iso:', 'csr:') in the message body, but no call-site attaches a structured `component` or `phase` attr via logger.With() — only `run_id` is pinned (tui.SetRunID). JSON consumers can filter by run_id but cannot filter `component=haproxy` because no such key exists. Phase constructors (setup/install/postinstall/destroy/cleanup) never narrow p.Log with `phase=install` or the component name.
evidence:
p.Log.Info(fmt.Sprintf("update-ingress: waiting for %s loadbalancer ip", svcName))
p.Log.Info("haproxy: removing vip", "vip", vip, "iface", iface)
logger.Warn("cleanup: failed to stop service", "svc", serviceName, "err", err)
// no p.Log = logger.With("phase", "postinstall", "component", "haproxy") anywhere
severity_reason: Pervasive field-stability issue — blocks JSON log filtering by component; not correctness. Keeping minor because the run_id correlation introduced since prior run narrows the practical impact.
fix_summary: At each phase constructor (setup/install/postinstall/destroy/cleanup) wrap p.Log via logger.With("phase", "install"); at sub-component boundaries (haproxy, dns, kubevip, terraform, iso, packages, cleanup.services, cleanup.packages, addon.manager) further narrow with logger.With("component", "haproxy"). Retain the human-readable prefix in the message for TTY users — tests and JSON consumers pick up the attr; the prefix is additive. This composes with the existing RedactHandler because WithAttrs propagates through the wrapper.
rule_source: Go log/slog design: stable keys, per-component WithAttrs
Google SRE, Structured Logging — 'fields are for machines, messages for humans'
repo-counter-example: internal/cli/helpers.go:L188 — tui.Info("starting deployment...", tui.LF("cluster", clusterFQDN)) shows the correct attr-based shape
must_preserve: The operator-visible prefix for TTY readability; the existing run_id pinned attr.

smell: WaitFor still emits `<prefix>: waiting (elapsed=30s)` at Info level on every ticker tick (default 30s). Across ~5 concurrent polling call sites (kubevip daemonset, kubevip port 6443, haproxy api-via-vip, flux controllers, addon verify) the Info stream drowns real state transitions during a 30-60 minute install. The 'waiting' line belongs at Debug; Info should fire once at start and once at ready. The prior audit flagged this — structured attrs were added but the level was not changed.
severity_reason: Signal-to-noise degradation; bounded at ~2 Info lines/minute per polling site. No correctness risk.
fix_summary: Change the per-tick line to logger.Debug. Keep the Info start/ready pair emitted by callers. If operator feedback matters for slow TTYs, emit Info at coarse intervals (every 5 minutes) via a lastNoticeAt timestamp. Spinner already covers TTY operators.
rule_source: Google SRE, Monitoring: log state transitions, not heartbeat
Go log/slog idiom: Debug for heartbeat
must_preserve: readyMsg Info line at ready; caller-emitted start Info line.

smell: Orchestrator.executeStep still does not emit a structured start/finish log pair per step. Skipping is logged (L90) but success/duration is not — Duration is captured in StepResult but never reaches the logger. Each phase's steps.go hand-rolls uneven OnStart/OnComplete log lines, so JSON consumers see inconsistent span boundaries. For a 60-minute install, missing per-step duration hurts post-mortem debugging.
severity_reason: Debuggability gap — missing per-step duration in structured stream. Not correctness.
fix_summary: In executeStep, before step.OnStart() log `o.logger.Info("step started", "step", step.ID(), "name", step.Name())`. After Execute (both success and error branches) log `o.logger.Info("step completed", "step", step.ID(), "duration", time.Since(startedAt), "success", err == nil)`. Keep level at Info or Debug per operator feedback; Debug is safer because OnStart/OnComplete already emit TTY-oriented lines.
rule_source: Go log/slog design: span boundaries at orchestration layer
repo-counter-example: internal/distribution/orchestrator.go:L90 — skip branch already logs structurally
must_preserve: Existing step.OnStart / step.OnComplete hand-rolled lines — new lines are additive.

smell: configureLogging still does not auto-select JSON format when stderr is not a TTY. Operators piping `okdctl deploy 2>&1 | jq .` get charmlog text with ANSI color escapes by default and must remember to pass `--log-format json`. Progress-bar suppression IS TTY-aware (L42) so the template for the fix exists in the same function. The log-level quiet/verbose sugar works via Changed() — the same approach would gate format auto-detection.
severity_reason: UX affordance; operators can pass --log-format json explicitly. Prior audit's findings stand.
fix_summary: Add a helper `cmd.Flags().Changed("log-format")` check (cobra PersistentPreRunE has cmd access). If not set and !stderrIsTTY, default logFormat to "json". Explicit --log-format wins. Alternatively: keep text but disable ANSI color when !stderrIsTTY by exposing a charmlog SetColorProfile call from tui.ConfigureLoggers. The existing progressBars gate at L42 is the template.
rule_source: CLI UX convention: auto-switch to machine format when piped
Go log/slog design: handler selection at main
repo-counter-example: internal/cli/logging.go:L42 — the TTY-aware path already exists for progress bars
must_preserve: --log-format flag takes precedence over auto-detection; --quiet/--verbose log-level sugar.

smell: secretstore.installPrereqCheck still logs a 7-line HOW-TO guide for each provider (onepassword: 6 Warn lines, vault: 3 Warn lines, bitwarden: 3 Warn lines) via env.Logger.Warn when credential files are missing. Warn is for recoverable degradation; this is user education. Structured log sinks (JSON / file) will record 6+ Warn entries per missing provider that an alerting rule will count as six distinct issues. This is operator-facing TTY guidance, not machine-oriented event data.
evidence:
env.Logger.Warn(fmt.Sprintf("secretstore: no secret files found in %s, skipping", dir))
env.Logger.Warn("secretstore: to set up 1password connect secrets:")
env.Logger.Warn("  1. download 1password-credentials.json from Settings > Automation in 1password.com")
env.Logger.Warn("  2. create a connect token and save it:")
// ... 4 more env.Logger.Warn lines
severity_reason: Level-discipline — Warn misused for help text, and duplicated per-provider. Not correctness.
fix_summary: Emit the first line ('no secret files found ... skipping') at Warn as the actual advisory. Print the numbered instructions via tui.Info (or a direct fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, ...) block) — operator-facing setup guidance belongs on the UX channel, not the structured log. Same pattern for vault and bitwarden providers.
rule_source: Go log/slog idiom: Warn for recoverable degradation, Info for state, fmt/tui for user UX
repo-counter-example: internal/cli/helpers.go:L51-L53 — setup hints go through tui.Info, not env.Logger.Warn
must_preserve: The help content — move channel, don't lose it.

smell: coreos.go logs `coreos: found existing iso at X` (L64, L78) and `coreos: iso already exists at X` (L206, L271) in four distinct sites. A single setup run can fire more than one of these for the same iso because the lookups happen across different layers (local iso dir, work-dir cache, download destination, upload destination), producing three nearly-identical Info lines. This is a log-once violation — same event announced repeatedly as the caller layers each do their own existence check.
severity_reason: Signal-to-noise; same event logged multiple times per run.
fix_summary: Consolidate the four sites into one helper (`logISOFound(path)`) that emits the Info line once per iso-path in a run — keep a set of already-logged paths keyed off filepath.Base. If the two message variants (found vs already-exists) carry distinct operator semantics, rename them so the distinction is readable.
rule_source: Google SRE, Structured Logging: log-once-per-event
Go proverb: clear is better than clever
must_preserve: Either variant's diagnostic value — the operator wants to see the iso was found, but not three times per setup.

smell: setup.installSystemPackages still logs `packages: <pkg> not found` and `packages: <pkg> already installed` at Info for every package — for a typical RHEL setup that's 4 sysPkgs (coreos-installer, haproxy, apache, dnsmasq), so ~4 Info lines of no-op state checks BEFORE the actual work. The 'already installed' outcome is a no-op; Info is reserved for state transitions. Matches the level-info-should-debug pattern.
severity_reason: Level-discipline — Info for no-op state checks.
fix_summary: Drop per-package Info lines. Emit a single Info line after the loop: `p.Log.Info("packages: scanned system packages", "missing", len(toInstall), "installed", len(sysPkgs)-len(toInstall))`. Move per-package detail to Debug if diagnostically useful.
rule_source: Go log/slog idiom: Debug for per-item trace, Info for per-batch state
must_preserve: The 'all system packages already installed' Info — it's the useful line.

smell: The per-VM site (L188) was migrated to structured form `"vm", name, "ip", ip` but three count-bearing lines remain unstructured: L158 `fmt.Sprintf("terraform: plan will create %d virtual machines", totalNodes)`, L185 `fmt.Sprintf("terraform: provisioned %d vms", len(result.VMs))`, L217 `fmt.Sprintf("terraform: plan will preview %d virtual machines", totalNodes)`. JSON consumers cannot index on `vm_count` because the number lives inside the message string. Partial resolution of the prior audit finding — sweep the count fields too.
evidence:
p.logger.Info(fmt.Sprintf("terraform: plan will create %d virtual machines", totalNodes))
...
p.logger.Info(fmt.Sprintf("terraform: provisioned %d vms", len(result.VMs)))
...
p.logger.Info(fmt.Sprintf("terraform: plan will preview %d virtual machines", totalNodes))
severity_reason: Field-stability — numeric fields wedged into message string. Prior audit resolved the per-vm case; this completes the sweep.
fix_summary: Replace with structured form: L158 → `p.logger.Info("terraform: plan calculated", "vm_count", totalNodes)`; L185 → `p.logger.Info("terraform: provisioned vms", "count", len(result.VMs))`; L217 → `p.logger.Info("terraform: plan preview", "vm_count", totalNodes)`. Keep the human-readable prefix in the message for TTY readability.
rule_source: Go log/slog design: typed attrs for machine consumers
repo-counter-example: internal/infrastructure/proxmox/proxmox.go:L188 — correct per-vm structured form

smell: MonitorInstallation's CSR approval tick runs every 30s for up to 60 minutes. On each tick: on error it Warns structured, on approved>0 it Infos structured. The error case correctly logs every tick (diagnostic value) but during a prolonged CSR endpoint outage the Warn stream can reach ~120 entries, all identical in root cause. This is the log-per-retry pattern at Warn level.
severity_reason: Bounded at 2 Warns/minute. Keeping as suggestion: during a genuine outage you want to see repeated failures, and de-duping risks hiding a slow-degrading endpoint.
fix_summary: Optional: de-dup identical consecutive Warns via a `lastWarnErrMsg` tracker, downgrading repeats to Debug after the first. Keep `approved>0` Info as-is (state transition). Only apply if operator feedback actually reveals noise — current severity-suggestion reflects that.
rule_source: Google SRE, Monitoring: log state changes, not constant failures
Go proverb: clear is better than clever
must_preserve: approved>0 Info — operators rely on seeing progress.

smell: executor.run still only logs `+ <name> <args>` at Debug when Verbose is true — nothing bookends the call in the structured stream. For a 15-minute terraform apply or oc poll the JSON sink sees nothing until completion. Cross-ref: prior-wave subprocess audit flagged buffered terraform output; observability owns the span-boundary half.
severity_reason: Operator feedback gap for JSON/file sinks; TTY is covered by spinner. Not correctness.
fix_summary: At start of executor.run log `e.logger.Debug("exec started", "cmd", name, "argc", len(args))` (omit argv itself — a terraform invocation argv can contain a credential substitution in rare configs). After cmd.Run log `e.logger.Debug("exec completed", "cmd", name, "exit", result.ExitCode, "duration", result.Duration)`. Keep at Debug so default verbosity is unchanged.
rule_source: Go log/slog design: span boundaries
Seam with subprocess audit (sub:4c092fce)
must_preserve: The Verbose-gated `+ name args` Debug line.

smell: tui.Debug/Info/Warn/Error write directly to the package-level stderrLogger (a charmlog.Logger) without routing through logutil.RedactHandler. Only tui.SimpleLogger() wraps the charmlog handler in NewRedactHandler. Every tui.X call site (63 occurrences across 9 files, including deploy/destroy/cleanup/debug_bundle) bypasses the redact sweep. If any future caller passes a cred-keyed LF (e.g. tui.LF("api_token", tok) or tui.LF("password", pw)) it writes raw to stderr/--log-file. CLAUDE.md §credentials-and-secrets explicitly names RedactHandler as the sink-side guard — but the guard only fires on slog.Logger traffic, not on tui.X direct-write traffic.
severity_reason: rubric §4/credential-exposure — latent sink-side bypass. Current call sites audit-clean (grep shows no tui.LF with a secret key), but CLAUDE.md §credentials-and-secrets names RedactHandler as the guarantee and this path sidesteps it. Installing the guard before a regression makes the contract structural, not by-inspection.
fix_summary: Route tui.Debug/Info/Warn/Error through the same RedactHandler path as SimpleLogger. Two approaches: (a) rewrite the helpers to construct a slog.Logger wrapping stderrLogger with RedactHandler once at package init, then fieldsToArgs-forward; (b) import logutil and have each helper apply redactAttr to LogField values before forwarding. Option (a) preserves the charmlog styled output because RedactHandler delegates to the inner handler. Write a table test that calls tui.Warn("…", tui.LF("password", "secret")) and asserts the stderr capture contains [redacted] — current RedactHandler tests don't cover the tui.X path.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §credentials-and-secrets — 'slog records pass through internal/logutil.RedactHandler (installed by tui.SimpleLogger)'
Seam #3 — observability owns the sink
repo-counter-example: internal/tui/logger.go:L109 — SimpleLogger wraps correctly; the same wrap is missing on L69-L78
must_preserve: charmlog styled output, stderr routing, tui.LF call signature. NopLogger is unaffected.

smell: When --log-file is set, configureLogging builds an io.MultiWriter(os.Stderr, f) and passes it to tui.ConfigureLoggers as stderrW. The charmlog.Logger's SetOutput then writes every record — INCLUDING all tui.Debug/Info/Warn/Error traffic and every SimpleLogger record — to the file. For SimpleLogger traffic this is fine because RedactHandler rewrites the slog.Record before it reaches charmlog. For tui.X traffic (see obs:660d83a5) the file receives un-redacted output. Result: --log-file amplifies the tui.X bypass by persisting it to disk at 0o600 (world-unreadable but still present on the host filesystem for debug-bundle collection).
severity_reason: rubric §4/credential-exposure — amplifies obs:660d83a5 by persisting the un-redacted bypass to a disk file that debug-bundle may later collect. Fixing obs:660d83a5 fixes this structurally; tracked separately so the log-file path is explicitly called out.
fix_summary: Same root-cause fix as obs:660d83a5: route tui.X through a logutil.RedactHandler-wrapped handler that is then bound to stderrLogger. Once the tui.X helpers go through RedactHandler, charmlog's SetOutput to the MultiWriter will receive already-redacted text. No change needed in cli/logging.go itself.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §credentials-and-secrets
Seam #3
repo-counter-example: internal/cli/debug_bundle.go:L35-L40 — the 'credentials are redacted' contract advertised by the debug-bundle Long description
must_preserve: The 0o600 file mode on the log file; append semantics.

smell: The two top-level error handlers stringify the error (`tui.Error(err.Error())`) before passing to the tui sink — so any structured error chain (errtypes.ClusterError wrapping a typed inner err, or a cancellation wrapped with %w) is collapsed to a single msg string. Once obs:660d83a5 routes tui.X through RedactHandler, stringification defeats the walk because RedactHandler operates on attrs, not on the free-form message. Mirror the structured form used in the rest of the repo: tui.Error("command failed", tui.LF("err", err)).
severity_reason: Field-stability — loses structured error info at the last log-site before the exit. Prior seam finding err:7b2829bb was resolved at executor/terraform; this is the one remaining root-level stringification.
fix_summary: Replace `tui.Error(err.Error())` with `tui.Error("command failed", tui.LF("err", err))` at both sites. Keep the exit-code logic unchanged. Once tui.X routes through RedactHandler (obs:660d83a5), passing the err as an attr lets the handler apply redactAny (Redacted() interface or *url.URL guard) — stringification pre-empties that.
rule_source: Go log/slog idiom: pass errors as structured attrs
repo-counter-example: internal/addon/manager.go:L98 — m.logger.Warn("addons: install and verify failed", "err", err)
Seam #3 — observability owns the sink half
must_preserve: The exit-code taxonomy; order of error-check vs ctx.Err check.
